statements.text: Climate variation is normal, so why should this be a problem?
Climate change will not be a problem because there will be technological solutions available.
I think it is safe to say climate change is here.
The negative effects of climate change on local commerce should be taken into account.
I do not trust what scientists say about climate change.
I do not trust what I hear about climate change from the government.
It is difficult to trust what comes out in the media on the issue of climate change.
There is not enough information to definitively say that climate change is real.
There is not much point in me doing anything to make agriculture more sustainable. No one else is going to.
I do not know what to do. I am very concerned and would like to do something, but I donâ€™t have a realistic shortlist of things that would really make a difference.
I believe that the difference we can have as an individual, in Switzerland, is so minimal that our actions are worthless.
I am not going to do anything to address the impacts of the agri-food system because it is not a major issue.
I am happy to pay a higher price for local or organic food products
Eating sustainably is too expensive, and only wealthy people can afford it
Agricultural subsidies should promote sustainable, pesticide and antibiotic-free production.
Sustainable agriculture increases prices and harms consumer freedom. The production should be adapted to what people demand.
Food accessibility (price) and security (availability) is NOT COMPATIBLE with a sustainable food system
Strong regulation of food production will eventually damage our economic relationship with other countries
We should develop short distribution channels and support local production instead of supporting big agrifood corporations
We need to focus on adaptation actions that are concerned with the economic future of the country.
Actions on the food system in Switzerland will lead to increased imports and a shift of pollution abroad
We need actions to protect inhabitants and biodiversity from harmful pesticides.
As long as we use animals in agriculture, it cannot be sustainable
We need to deal with the water pollution issue through measures such as reducing fertilizer and pesticide use.
Banning pesticides might help the local biodiversity but decreases our food production capacity and autonomy
Agriculture is already very sustainable. Swiss farmers are on the right track
Intensive food production can go along with the protection of the environment and health
Farmers already suffer enough from strict rules and paperwork. Family farmers should have more liberties
The main focus of planning for adaptation should be to prepare the food system for extreme weather events, such as drought and flooding.
Products that use environmentally harmful ingredients, such as palm oil, should be taxed in the same way as tobacco products.
If Switzerland reduces greenhouse gas emissions in its food system, it wonâ€™t make a difference.
It is important to plan for migration by people displaced by malnutrition and famine.
We should focus on protecting human systems rather than environmental ecosystems.
The Swiss food system depends on imports from other countries, and it is in our interest to help find an effective global solution.
Some communities are more affected than others by the global agri-food system, but this is not a priority issue.
The Swiss food system is particularly vulnerable to climate change, and it is in our interest to help find an effective global solution.
Climate warming will ultimately benefit food production globally as plants better growth in higher temperature
It is NOT necessary to engage with the community when deciding what are the most important issues for planning for food system changes.
Planning for food system adaptation needs a holistic approach, considering a whole range of issues, instead of focusing on individual issues.
There is no urgent need to prepare for an increase in illness and death caused by intensive use of pesticides/antibiotics
The community should be involved in discussions about food system adaptation.
It is important to support small-land local farming as they have the fewest resources to deal with the impacts of climate change.
Leave the policy settings as they are.
Policies that emphasise fewer regulations (e.g., policies that promote free trade agreements by reducing food regulation)
Policies that involve moderate sustainable regulations (e.g., banning certain types of pesticides, incentivising organic agriculture)

Policies that involve a radical sustainable food regulation (e.g., banning all pesticides, banning the importation of food-related products that employ non-sustainable approaches, exclusively incentivising organic agriculture)
Policies that create incentives for local producers to produce sustainable food (e.g., subsidies or tax breaks for local farmers who produce organic products)
Adaptation policies and expenditure. Planning controls and emergency response programs.
Preparing for climate risk for food production through the development of new approaches and technologies that enhance resilience to the impacts of climate variability or change.
